result.title: Sliding Networks: A Family of Residual Structures Preserving Feature Learning and Feature Diversity
result.summary: Deep learning models tend to perform best at large widths and depths. The growing interest in scaling laws, especially in the language modeling domain, has motivated procedures for scaling up network widths and depths in order to preserve stability and computational efficiency of training dynamics. Existing depth-scaling approaches force a choice between retaining locally maximal \emph{feature learning} and preserving a form of \emph{feature diversity} in the residual stream arising from random differences between channels. We examine a \textit{joint scaling recipe} that preserves both. With residual width $N_\flat$, hidden width $N_\sharp$, and depth $L$, the key quantity is, by default, the limiting ratio $N_\flat/(N_\sharp L)\toα$, while correlated initialization (Half Copy) can partially relax the resulting shape constraints. Theory and residual-MLP experiments support convergence at fixed positive $α$ to an SDE limit with locally maximal feature learning. Hidden computations can then be redistributed between width and depth while preserving this limit, like turning melody into harmony and back. Language-model experiments nevertheless show performance differences under regrouping at fixed parameter count. These results distinguish approximating a limit (ODE or SDE) from scaling for better performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一族「sliding」残差结构，通过联合缩放残差宽度、隐藏宽度与深度（默认约束 N_flat/(N_sharp·L)→α，并可用 Half Copy 相关初始化放宽），在保持局部最大特征学习的同时保留残差流中的特征多样性，并从理论与残差 MLP 实验给出 SDE 极限分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「残差流特征多样性—特征学习权衡」与深度/宽度重分配分析，可供核查 LVR 中多层 latent 推理状态是否随深度发生信息坍缩、以及宽度与深度如何分担推理计算；论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
